correctness.rationale: The exact independent-choice construction and precise zero-child definition fix all quantifiers for n≥3. The i<j joint root/terminal event gives Cov(A_j,B_i)=(n-j)q^(n-i-1)/(n-1)^2, with zero for j≤i; summing and differentiating a finite geometric series gives the stated covariance. Conditional on independent Bernoulli root flags and fixed older-parent targets, both counts are increasing coordinatewise; an elementary induction proves product-measure positive association, with explicit pivotal event for strictness. Exact two-terminal joint probabilities imply the variance formula, and uniform Taylor expansions control both asymptotic Riemann sums and yield the positive correlation constant. A standalone fully independent exact enumeration checks 425 identities/inequalities over 50,068 configurations; the unrestricted proof does not rely on those finite checks.

originality.rationale: Originality is relative to the inspected and available record. The focal source [arXiv:1906.08806, sections 2.2, 3.1, 4.1] contains the independent-choice forest representation, the component-count law, and the individual degree marginal; these are prior inputs. It does not state the root–zero-child-terminal cross-covariance kernel, all-monotone positive association, exact finite covariance, or nonzero correlation limit. Published-result comparisons on recursive-tree root degree/leaves and Cayley endpoint degree/distance are distinct stochastic models and their statements do not imply the Moran-forest theorem. The older uniform recursive-forest paper has a different forest sampling law and was not accessible in full; implicit historical derivations remain a material caveat.
residual_risks: A prior paper may implicitly derive the same mixed covariance from the known independent-choice Moran construction, even if the inspected focal paper does not display it.

value.rationale: Fragmentation (component count) and zero-child lineage extinction (terminal count) are natural different observables of the stationary Moran genealogy. Previous marginal descriptions do not quantify their joint fluctuations. The complete triangular cross-covariance kernel establishes how later root formation preserves earlier terminality, with positive covariance under every increasing transform. Its exact finite covariance and a nonvanishing ~0.630879 correlation contrast sharply with negative pairwise terminal correlations. This is a model-wide dependence and fluctuation result, not an arbitrary small finite statistic or a renamed marginal.
